title: Cloud Encryption and Key Rotation Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:config:notification` events with `configRuleList{}.configRuleName=*encryption*` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.11 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:config:notification` traffic without `configRuleList{}.configRuleName=*encryption*`. Confirm UC-4.4.11 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via Config/Security Hub, Defender, SCC, or CSPM; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Config/Security Hub, Defender, SCC, or CSPM
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleList{}.configRuleName=*encryption*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.11_cloud_encryption_and_key_11"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.11 — Cloud Encryption and Key Rotation Compliance: queries Microsoft Azure `aws:config:notification` for search criteria `configRuleList{}.configRuleName=*encryption*` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Cloud Encryption and Key Rotation Compliance' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.11 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Use native compliance (Config rules, Azure Policy, SCC) or CSPM to evaluate encryption and key rotation. Ingest findings. Dashboard non-compliant resources by rule and cloud. Alert on new non-compliant critical resources.
visualization: Table (resource, rule, cloud, status), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (non-compliant by rule).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Config/Security Hub, Defender, SCC, or CSPM with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use native compliance (Config rules, Azure Policy, SCC) or CSPM to evaluate encryption and key rotation. Ingest findings. Dashboard non-compliant resources by rule and cloud. Alert on new non-compliant critical resources.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleList{}.configRuleName=*encryption*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.11_cloud_encryption_and_key_11"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect cloud encryption and key rotation compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_11_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (resource, rule, cloud, status), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart (non-compliant by rule)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Config/Security Hub, Defender, SCC, or CSPM and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud encryption and key rotation compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
